readerTitle: Why winning at home doesn't mean winning next door
caseNote: 실제 기업 (Target의 캐나다 진출과 철수, 2013~2015) + 가상 적용 (청소 서비스, 기장·회계 서비스)
insight: 새 시장에 들어갈 때는 '우리가 무엇을 잘하나'가 아니라 '우리를 이기게 해 준 조건 중 무엇을 가져갈 수 있나'를 묻는다.
misconception: 본거지에서 통한 방식이면 다른 지역이나 다른 고객층에서도 그대로 통한다. 선점하려면 처음부터 크게 들어가야 한다.

sources.text: Target Corporation press release (January 15, 2015): Target to discontinue operations in Canada
Castaldo, J. (2016). The Last Days of Target. Canadian Business.

factChecks.note: Target은 2013년 3월 캐나다 첫 매장을 열었고 2013년 말까지 120곳 이상(약 124곳)을 열었으며, 철수 발표 시점(2015년 1월) 매장 수는 약 133곳입니다. 카드에는 "more than 120 stores in under a year", "less than two years after the first store opened"로 적었습니다. 게시 전 Target 공식 자료로 재확인하세요.
빈 진열대, 미국 매장보다 높은 가격, 새 물류·재고 시스템의 데이터 문제는 언론 보도(Canadian Business 2016 등)로 널리 알려진 내용입니다. 손실액 등 구체 수치는 출처마다 달라 카드에 넣지 않았습니다.
Target이 캐나다 매장 상당수를 기존 Zellers 매장 임차권을 인수해 열었다는 점은 카드에 넣지 않았습니다. 추가하려면 인수 금액과 시점을 1차 자료로 확인하세요.
청소 서비스, 기장·회계 서비스 사례는 설명용 가상 사례이며 수치를 쓰지 않았습니다.

cards.title: Why winning at home doesn't mean winning next door
body: In 2013, Target, one of America's biggest retailers, crossed the border into Canada. It opened more than 120 stores in under a year.
Less than two years after the first store opened, the company announced it would close every one of them.

image.label: Rows of new stores with empty shelves
image.brief: 3D 클레이 스타일. 새로 지은 대형 매장 안, 반짝이는 바닥과 밝은 조명인데 진열대는 대부분 비어 있음. 실제 기업 로고, 빨간 과녁 마크, 상표는 절대 쓰지 않음.

cards.title: Your cleaning company wants a second city.
body: Your house-cleaning business is the best-reviewed in your city. Most new customers come from referrals, and your crews know every neighborhood.
A bigger city two hours away has no clear leader. How do you go in?

options.text: Launch big: ten crews, heavy ads, same prices as home
options.feedback: You'd grab attention fast. But you'd be paying full size for a market where nobody knows you and you don't yet know the streets, prices or hiring pool.

options.text: Start with two crews in one district and learn what works
options.feedback: Slower to grow, but cheap to fix. You find out which of your strengths survive the move before you bet on all of them.

options.text: Undercut local cleaners on price to win customers quickly
options.feedback: Low prices can replace the referrals you don't have yet. But they train customers to expect cheap, and they don't test whether your service wins on its own.

cards.title: The name traveled. The machine didn't.
body: Many Canadians already knew Target from shopping trips across the border. They arrived expecting full shelves and US prices.

Instead, many stores had gaps on the shelves. A new supply and inventory system, built quickly for a whole country at once, struggled to get the right goods to the right stores. Prices were often higher than shoppers remembered.
Target had decades to build its system at home. In Canada it had to build one while running more than a hundred stores.

cards.title: Some advantages travel. Some stay home.
body: **Entering a new market** means selling to a new place or a new group of customers. The trap is assuming everything that made you win comes with you.

Some advantages travel: know-how, methods, a well-known name. Others are tied to the home market: your supplier network, local relationships, referrals, and years of knowing what customers there want.
Target brought its brand and its store format. The parts that kept shelves full stayed behind.

image.label: A suitcase holding some strengths, others left behind
image.brief: 여행 가방 하나. 가방 안에는 "Know-how", "Methods", "Brand name" 라벨이 붙은 블록. 가방 밖 바닥에 남겨진 블록에는 "Suppliers", "Relationships", "Referrals", "Local knowledge". 따뜻한 색감, 로고 없음.

cards.title: Three questions before you enter.
body: Before committing to a new market, sort your strengths honestly.
list: **What depends on things we can't bring?** Suppliers, people, reputation with real customers.
**What will customers there compare us to?** A local rival, or their memory of us somewhere else.
**What is the smallest move that tests our weakest point?** One district, one product line, a handful of customers.
cards.callout: Enter where you can learn fast and fix mistakes cheaply. Then scale what works.
cards.softwareNote: A software product can go live in a new country overnight, but the code is the part that travels easily. Local payment methods, language, data rules and sales relationships have to be rebuilt, and they're usually where launches stall.

cards.title: A famous name can raise the bar.
body: A known brand seems like a head start. It can also be a promise you have to keep from day one.
Unknown newcomers get some patience. Target didn't, because shoppers compared each store to the ones they'd visited in the US. The gap between expectation and experience became the story.
When your reputation arrives before you do, the first months matter more, not less.

cards.title: Small and slow has costs too.
body: A small test can mislead. Some businesses only work at scale: a delivery network or a chain of stores may lose money at three locations and profit at thirty.
Rivals can also move while you're testing. And in some markets, suppliers or big customers won't take you seriously until you commit.
The point isn't to always start small. It's to know which of your advantages you're betting on, and test the shakiest one first.

cards.title: Now it's a bookkeeping firm.
body: Your firm does bookkeeping and payroll for about 200 restaurants. Owners refer each other, and you know their cash flow problems by heart.
You want to start serving dental clinics. What do you do first?

options.feedback: That proof means a lot to restaurant owners and little to dentists. Your referral network is an advantage that stays home.

options.text: Take on three clinics at a fair price and learn how their finances differ
options.feedback: You give up quick growth, but you learn what dentists need that restaurants don't, like insurance billing, before you build a whole service line.

options.text: Hire a salesperson from the dental industry and launch a full package
options.feedback: This buys local relationships, a real gap. But you'd be selling a package before you know whether your service fits clinics.

cards.title: Before you enter, check what you can actually bring.
body: Your skills may travel. Your suppliers, relationships and reputation often don't. Enter in a way that tests the weakest of those first.
**Try it today:** list three reasons customers choose you now. Next to each, write whether it would still be true in the market you'd enter next.
